title: Protocol to dissociate and isolate wide-diversity single cells by density gradient centrifugation from human hepatoblastoma tissue
protocol: Select tissue from the area of interest, trim as much of the discarded tissue as possible with a sterile scalpel and cut the tissue to a size of about 6 mm.
Wash the tissue twice with pre-cooled PBS or cell suspension solution.
Place the tissue in tissue storage solution and transport on ice for further experiments within 30 min.
Remove tissue from tissue preservation solution and place on ice in a 35 mm Petri dish.
Rinse tissue 2–3 times using ice-cold PBS or cell suspension solution to remove any remaining blood.
Trim tissue blocks in PBS with sterilized scissors, selecting structurally intact tissue with a weight of about 0.2 g and avoiding blood clots.
Aspirate the PBS and unwanted tissue.
Gently cut the tissue with scissors into 1 mm³ dimension.
Aspirate 5 mL of cell lysis solution using a serological pipette.
Add the cell lysis solution to the Petri dish containing the tissue.
Transfer the tissue and solution into a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Place the tube in a 37°C water bath shaker set at 80–100 rpm.
Digest the tissue for 8 minutes.
Pipette the tissue and liquid up and down about 10 times using a 5 mL Pasteur pipette.
Collect the suspension after settling of remaining tissue.
Discharge the suspension onto a 70 μm cell strainer placed on ice to collect cells.
Rinse the cell strainer with about 200 μL of cell suspension solution.
Pass the cell suspension through the cell strainer to retrieve the maximal number of cells.
Add 5 mL of fresh cell lysis solution into the remaining tissue fragments in the 50 mL centrifuge tube for a second round of tissue dissociation.
Incubate the mixture in a 37°C water bath for 10 min.
Shake the centrifuge tube every 2 min for 5–10 s during incubation.
Transfer the suspension to the 50 mL centrifuge tube from which the supernatant was previously collected and stored when digestion is complete.
Repeat the enzymatic digestion of the tissue precipitate in step 2 and collect the supernatant if necessary.
Filter all collected supernatant through a 70 μm filter.
Collect the filtrate using a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the collected filtrate at 300 g for 6 min at 4°C to collect the cells.
Resuspend the cell precipitate using cell suspension solution.
Transfer the resuspended cells to a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Repeat the previous centrifugation step.
Resuspend the precipitate with an appropriate amount of ice-cold cell suspension solution or PBS (∼2–3 mL).
Add 3 mL of the 30% Percoll solution to the bottom of a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Using a Pasteur pipette, reach to the bottom of the tube and slowly add 3 mL of the 50% Percoll solution to the lower layer of the 30% Percoll solution.
Slowly add 3 mL of the cell suspension onto the surface of the 30% Percoll layer without disturbing the gradient.
Aspirate and discard the top layer of PBS from the density gradient.
Discard the cellular debris layer between the PBS and 30% Percoll layer.
Discard the 30% Percoll layer in turn.
Carefully transfer the hepatocyte layer between the 30% Percoll layer and 50% Percoll layer to a 15 mL centrifuge tube, keeping the total volume to a maximum of 2 mL.
Dilute the cell suspension of the hepatocyte layer with three times its volume in cell suspension solution.
Centrifuge the diluted cell suspension at 300 g for 10 min at 4°C.
Aspirate and discard all supernatants remaining below the 50% Percoll layer.
Resuspend the immune cell precipitate using 1 mL of ACK Lysing buffer.
Let the mixture react for 3 minutes at room temperature to lyse erythrocytes.
Fill the erythrocyte lysed immune cell fluid with 10 mL of cell suspension solution in a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the sample at 500 g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Resuspend the cell precipitates from steps 20 and 22 respectively with 2 mL of cell suspension solution or 0.04% BSA solution.
Perform quality control on the cell suspensions, including viability, concentration, and singularity evaluation and counting.
Examine and record the activity of the immune cell resuspension and hepatocyte layer suspension under a microscope.
Combine the two cell suspensions and quantify them.
Aspirate 10 μL of Percoll density gradient centrifuged hepatocyte layer suspension.
Stain the aspirated hepatocyte sample with 10 μL of Trypan blue stain (0.4%).
Aspirate 10 μL of immune cell resuspension after erythrocyte lysis.
Stain the aspirated immune cell sample with 10 μL of Trypan blue stain (0.4%).
Examine the stained samples using ECLIPSE Ti2 inverted microscope.
Mix the hepatocyte suspension and immune cell suspension together.
Centrifuge the mixed single cell suspensions at 400 g for 10 min at 4°C.
Resuspend the pelleted cells in 5 mL of cell suspension solution or 0.04% BSA solution.
Proceed to detect the viability and concentration of the single cell suspensions.
Stain 10 μL of the final single-cell suspension with 10 μL of Cellometer ViaStainTM AOPI Staining Solution.
Analyze the stained sample using the Countstar Altair Smart Cell Analyzer.
Determine cell viability and concentration based on the automated counts.
Ensure the live cell concentration is at least 80% to proceed further.
Proceed to the next step if both cell viability is ≥ 80% and cell count is ≥ 500 cells/mL.
Set the correct focus on an automated cell counter to count all surviving cells of different sizes and shapes.
Examine cell morphology under a bright-field microscope for a quick visual inspection.
Load cells onto Chromium Chip G using Chromium Controller to generate GEMs with the target of recovering 10000 cells.
Transfer GEMs to a new 0.2 mL centrifuge tube at the end of this step.
Execute the GEM-RT incubation procedure: Incubate at 53°C for 45 min, then at 85°C for 5 min, and hold at 4°C with lid temperature set at 53°C.
Store the products of GEM-RT Incubation at 4°C for up to 72 hours or at -20°C for up to a week.
Perform recovery, amplification, and purification of reverse transcription products according to the detailed operating manual.
Amplify cDNA using 11 PCR cycles as targeted cell recovery is between 6000 and 10000.
Purify amplified cDNA using AMPure XP beads.
Determine the concentration of purified cDNA using the Qubit™ dsDNA HS Assay Kit.
Fragment, end-repair, size-select, and ligate adapters to the cDNA according to the manual.
Amplify and purify the library using 12–14 PCR cycles depending on the input amount of cDNA (between 25–150 ng).
Purify amplified libraries using AMPure XP beads.
Determine the concentration of purified libraries using the Qubit™ dsDNA HS Assay Kit.
Dilute 1 μL sample with 9 μL water.
Load 1 μL of diluted DNA library on an Agilent Bioanalyzer High Sensitivity chip.
Select the region encompassing 35–10,000 bp and record the DNA concentration.
Pause point: Libraries can be frozen at −20°C or −80°C for several months.
Dilute each DNA library down to 2 nM concentration using 10 mM Tris-HCl [pH 8.5].
Pool individual DNA libraries into one tube.
Denature and dilute pooled libraries according to the NovaSeq 6000 Denature and Dilute Libraries Guide (Standard Loading).
Sequence the DNA library using NovaSeq 6000 S4 Reagent Kit v1.5 (300 cycles) with the following cycle recommendations: Read1, 28 cycles; i7 index, 10 cycles; i5 index, 10 cycles; Read 2, 90 cycles.
Aim for sequencing depth of 30,000–50,000 reads per cell or 120–200 million reads per DNA library.
Run Cellranger counts, process raw FASTQ data by alignment, filtering, barcode counts and UMI counts and generate single cell feature counts for a single library.
Load the required packages and data
library(dplyr)
library(Seurat)
Load data into R using the Read10X function from the Seurat package.
Create a Seurat object from the loaded data, setting the project name and minimum cells and features.
Visualize gene expression, reads, and mitochondrial expression using VlnPlot() function.
Calculate the percentage of mitochondrial genes for each cell.
Filter cells based on nFeature_RNA, nCount_RNA, and percent.mt thresholds.
Normalize the dataset using NormalizeData function with LogNormalize method.
Identify highly variable features in the normalized data.
Downscale and cluster the data using ScaleData(), FindNeighbors(), FindClusters(), and RunUMAP() functions in R.
Linearly transform the dataset for Principal Component Analysis (PCA) using the ScaleData() function with all genes as features.
Determine the data dimensions for further analysis after running PCA on HBdata.
Visualize the dataset using the RunUMAP() method.
Identify the cell types of the main cell clusters.
Separate different cell clusters using the subset() function for further identification of fine cell types.
